title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed and hand-corrected galley of an EGA IV draft (page 'IV-977-22'), section (18.13.4). It sits inside a folder on crystals and de Rham cohomology. The context, from (18.13.2), is a k-algebra A that is analytic, i.e. a quotient of a convergent or formal power series ring. For such A one has a 'finite' module of differentials Ω̄¹_{A/k}. The deleted clause recalled that this module is finitely generated. The page restates (18.13.2) categorically: in the category of finitely generated A-modules, Ω̄¹_{A/k} represents the covariant functor L ↦ Dér(A,L). The handwritten reference is (0_III, 8.1.11).

The page then generalizes. Let A be a topological ring and B a topological A-algebra that is a noetherian semi-local ring with its 𝔯-preadic topology (𝔯 the radical of B). A marginal note says this should be generalized to more general morphisms of topological rings.

(i) Every A-derivation D: B → L into a finitely generated B-module is automatically continuous for the 𝔯-preadic topologies. By Leibniz, D(𝔯^{j+1}) ⊂ 𝔯^j L.
(ii) Hence, by (0,20.4.8), D = u∘d_{B/A} with u: Ω¹_{B/A} → L B-linear. The map u is automatically continuous, since the canonical topology on Ω¹_{B/A} is the 𝔯-preadic one (0,20.4.5).
(iii) Define Ω̄¹_{B/A} as Ω¹_{B/A} modulo the intersection N of the kernels of all maps Ω¹_{B/A} → L with L finitely generated. Since L is noetherian, the image of such a map is finitely generated. So N is equivalently the intersection of the submodules M with Ω¹/M finitely generated.
(iv) Put d̄ = π∘d_{B/A}. This is an A-derivation, and its values generate Ω̄¹ (0,20.4.7).
(v) Conclusion (18.13.4.1): Hom_B(Ω̄¹_{B/A}, L) ≅ Dér_A(B,L) = Dér.cont_A(B,L), functorially in finitely generated L.

The page breaks off where the text begins to say that, under the hypotheses of (18.13.2), the newly defined Ω̄¹ coincides with the earlier one. In modern terms this is the construction of the universally finite (or 'finite') module of differentials, in the generality of semi-local noetherian algebras over a topological base. The purpose is to obtain a finitely generated substitute for the huge Kähler module Ω¹_{B/A} in analytic or complete situations, for use with de Rham complexes of formal or analytic algebras.
errors: Gap: the definition shows Hom_B(Ω̄¹,L) = Hom_B(Ω¹,L) for finitely generated L. But Ω̄¹ only represents the functor *within the category of finitely generated modules* if Ω̄¹ is itself finitely generated, and that is not shown. Ω¹/N embeds into a product of finitely generated modules but need not be finitely generated. Grothendieck evidently noticed this: he struck out the clause asserting finiteness in the analytic case. The existence of a universally finite differential module genuinely needs extra hypotheses, as in Scheja–Storch and Kunz.

Minor: in the first sentence the subscript of Dér for Ω̄¹_{A/k} should be k (Dér_k(A,L)). The handwritten correction reads as 'A' in the transcription, which would be inconsistent with A being the algebra; this is probably a transcription or reading issue.

ideas.what: Automatic continuity of derivations of a semi-local noetherian ring into finitely generated modules, via D(𝔯^{j+1}) ⊂ 𝔯^j L
ideas.modern_name: automatic continuity of derivations for adic topologies

ideas.what: Ω̄¹_{B/A} = Ω¹ modulo the intersection of all submodules with finitely generated quotient, representing Dér_A(B,−) on finitely generated modules
ideas.where_published: not in the published EGA IV §18, as far as I know; published EGA IV_4 §18 appears to stop before an analytic-differentials section 18.13 (unsure)

ideas.what: Finite differential module of an analytic k-algebra, represented in finitely generated modules

missed.claim: An unpublished EGA IV draft section (18.13) builds the universally finite differential module Ω̄¹_{B/A} for a semi-local noetherian algebra over an arbitrary topological ring. It identifies Dér_A(B,L) = Dér.cont_A(B,L) = Hom(Ω̄¹,L) for finitely generated L. This anticipates the Scheja–Storch/Kunz notion, which is not usually traced to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Nous désignerons par Ω̄¹_{B/A} le quotient de Ω¹_{B/A} par l'intersection des noyaux des homomorphismes Ω¹_{B/A} → L pour les B-modules L de type fini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: it shows the universally finite differential module was planned for EGA IV in the 1960s, in the context of de Rham and crystalline cohomology of formal or analytic algebras.

missed.claim: Marginal programme to extend the construction to more general morphisms of topological rings. The finiteness of Ω̄¹ in this generality is left unproved, and the claim was in fact deleted.
missed.quote: à généraliser au cas d'un homomorphisme d'anneaux topologiques plus général
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The existence and finiteness of universally finite differentials for general topological or adic morphisms remains a technical issue, e.g. for de Rham complexes of formal schemes.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically routine, with a finiteness gap the author himself flagged. The interest is mainly documentary: an unpublished EGA IV §18.13 draft on universally finite (analytic) differentials, predating the standard references (Scheja–Storch, Kunz).
transcription_corrections: Header: '- IV- 977 - 22 -' (the numbers 977 and 22 are handwritten).
In the first displayed functor the subscript of Dér should read k (Dér_k(A,L)); the handwritten mark is ambiguous.
Left margin note is roughly 'à généraliser au cas d'un homomorphisme d'anneaux topologiques plus général'.
Second margin note: 'On a donc Hom_B(Ω̄¹_{B/A},L) = Hom_B(Ω¹_{B/A},L) pour tout B-module de type fini L.'
The map labelled 'r' in the composite B → Ω¹ → Ω̄¹ is a handwritten π (projection).
